thread:
Anna (arch): Quick sync — proposing a compact 'alias' entry in rollout manifests to map stable names to concrete model versions. Want a quick design check before I open a PR.
Mike R: Sketch the minimal fields? my main worry is older clients silently ignoring new fields.
Anna (arch): Minimal: name, target, optional expires, alias_affects_cache (bool), compat_hint. Example manifest:
```json
{
  "release_id": "r-2026-03-22-1",
  "aliases": [
    {"name": "stable-embedding-v1", "target": "model-20260322-emb-q4", "expires": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z", "alias_affects_cache": true}
  ],
  "compat_policy": "shim",
  "soft_fallback_order": ["model-20260322-emb-q4", "model-20260201-emb-q3"]
}
```
Sasha L: Hmm. Can we piggyback on tags or labels instead of new top-level field?
Anna (arch): Tags are ambiguous. We need deterministic semantics for routing + cache keys + audit. Also want servers to emit headers to indicate alias resolution.
Jordan K: If alias_affects_cache=true and target flips mid-rollout, won't that blow through caches?
Anna (arch): Yes. That's intentional when teams need alias-level isolation. Default alias_affects_cache=false to avoid perf regressions. If true, infra appends "alias=<name>" to cache keys and to matcache tags.
Mike R: Backcompat plan? We can't force clients to parse new headers.
Anna (arch): Opt-in. Two ways: client header `Prefer-Alias: 1` or query `alias=true`. We'll also add a feature flag to flip default later. Servers must keep returning legacy X-Model-Version header to avoid regressions.
Sasha L: Telemetry: we need an event for alias resolution so we can measure traffic that followed alias mapping.
Anna (arch): Agreed. Emit compact events: 
```
alias.resolve { alias: "stable-embedding-v1", resolved_to: "model-20260322-emb-q4", client: "client-123", method: "Prefer-Alias" }
```
Mike R: What about rollout canaries? If a canary uses alias, and it's sticky, we need a way to pin at request level.
Anna (arch): Add optional per-request 'alias_pin' in response headers when a client should continue using same target for a short window; also an 'alias_ttl' seconds value. Can be advisory.
Jordan K: Any security/audit concerns? Need to persist alias->target history for later blames.
Anna (arch): Yes — alias changes will produce an audit entry: who changed it, when, previous target, reason. We'll tie to release_id. Also add signature on manifest for integrity.
deploy-bot: Release r-2026-03-22-1 created by @Anna (arch) — aliases: [stable-embedding-v1 -> model-20260322-emb-q4].
Mike R: Ok, looks reasonable. Can you enumerate migration tasks for the PR?
Anna (arch): 1) schema docs + manifest examples; 2) server: alias resolution + cache key toggles + headers; 3) client SDK: opt-in header + header parsing; 4) telemetry + audit logging; 5) rollout playbook. I'll open PR with these steps. Any blockers?
Sasha L: Make sure the alias_affects_cache default=false is explicit in docs. Also note that some CDNs may normalize query params — we should recommend header opt-in where possible.
Anna (arch): Good catch. Will add.
Jordan K: +1 on audit trail and signature. Otherwise lgtm.
Mike R: lgtm too, please add a short compatibility test matrix in PR.
Anna (arch): Will do, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
